venue.name: Horticulture Centre of the Pacific
venue.description: The Gardens at HCP are over nine acres of display gardens on a 103 acre site in Saanich, just outside Victoria, set in a conservation park with nature trails, wetlands and bird watching sites. The site runs HCP Kids, a set of land based programs that use the gardens and the surrounding forest as the classroom, and it also houses the Pacific Horticulture College. School programs run 1.5 hours, cover preschool through grade 12, and include entrance to the gardens, with an optional 30 minute self guided activity for an extra fee. The gardens are open daily from 9am to 4pm and children under 16 get in free.

facility_notes.washrooms: Access to the lower classroom portable for the bathroom, snack, storytime and warming up.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Pack a picnic and find a shady nook.
facility_notes.rain_backup: This program is based outside, rain or shine, with access to the lower classroom portable for the bathroom, snack, storytime and warming up or for those extra stormy days.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Most pathways are wheelchair and stroller friendly, but you may need extra time or assistance in sloped areas.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Most pathways are wheelchair and stroller friendly, but you may need extra time or assistance in sloped areas.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Buses may drop off and pick up passengers but cannot park in the lot due to space constraints. Limited parking may be available on Quayle Road.

restrictions: Youths and children must be supervised
Stay on paths and be respectful of our plants
Do not step on or reach into flower beds
Do not pick flowers or fruit
Pets must be leashed, under control at all times, and cleaned up after
Smoking and vaping of any kind are not permitted anywhere on the premises.
venue.hours_notes: Monday to Sunday, 9:00am to 4:00pm. The Gardens may be closed on statutory holidays, in inclement weather resulting in unsafe pathways, and from late December through early January. Touring the Gardens takes approximately one hour.
venue.seasonal_notes: The school programming page says classes are welcomed through the year, in fall, winter and spring.

programs.name: Garden Creatures
programs.description: A 1.5 hour facilitated visit in the gardens for preschool to grade 2, looking for the worms, snails, birds and snakes that live there and talking about what they need to survive and how to help their habitat. Program fees include entrance into the gardens. An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens can be added for an additional fee. The site publishes no dollar amount for any school program.
programs.what_children_do: Walk into the gardens with a facilitator and hunt for the animals that live there, worms, snails, birds and snakes, then talk about who they are and what each one needs to survive.
programs.our_note: Ninety minutes outdoors is a real stretch for three and four year olds, so plan for boots and layers whatever the forecast. No price is published for school visits, so ask for a quote and settle whether the extra half hour in the gardens is worth adding.
programs.practical_summary: There are washrooms on site and most paths take strollers, though the sloped parts take longer. Buses can drop off but cannot park, and the price, the group size limit and how much notice they need are all unpublished, so call first.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.

programs.name: Sensing the Seasons
programs.description: A 1.5 hour facilitated visit for preschool to grade 2 in which children use their senses in the gardens, smelling flowers, watching bees, listening to birds, touching soil and sometimes tasting something. The site says there is something to discover in the garden in any season. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the gardens with a facilitator using one sense at a time, smelling flowers, watching for bees, listening for birds, putting hands in the soil and sometimes tasting something growing there.
programs.our_note: This is the gentlest of their preschool options because it works in short bursts rather than one long walk. Ask what is actually in season on your date, since a February visit and a June visit are very different outings.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers. The price, the group size limit and the notice they need are not published anywhere, so a call is the only way to plan properly.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.

programs.name: More than Worms!
programs.description: A 1.5 hour facilitated visit for preschool to grade 5 about the animals, bacteria and fungi that break organic matter down into soil. The page says to get ready to get your hands dirty. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Dig into the garden soil with a facilitator to find the worms and the other creatures at work in it, and look at how bacteria and fungi turn dead plants into soil.
programs.our_note: This one gets genuinely muddy, so send a change of clothes and warn parents the day before. It spans preschool to grade 5, so ask them to pitch it for your youngest child rather than the middle of the range.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers. Nothing about the price, the maximum group size or the notice period is on the site, so plan a phone call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.
curriculum_tags: First Peoples concepts of interconnectedness in the environment
First Peoples knowledge of sustainable practices

programs.name: All You Seed is Love
programs.description: A 1.5 hour hands on program for preschool to grade 5 on the plant life cycle, covering seed starting, transplanting and the basics of plant propagation. The site says each student gets to plant seeds and take them home. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Fill and sow their own seed container, practise transplanting a seedling, and carry the planted seeds home at the end.
programs.our_note: Every child leaves holding something, which makes the bus ride home easier and gives the classroom a follow up for weeks afterwards. Ask what the seedlings need once they are back with you, because a tray of pots is a commitment.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers. The price, the group size limit and the notice they need are not published, so call to pin those down before you commit.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.
curriculum_tags: First Peoples concepts of interconnectedness in the environment
programs.evidence: All You Seed is Love (Preschool to Grade 5)

programs.name: School Gardens 101
programs.description: A 1.5 hour program for preschool to grade 7 about running a school garden, covering what to plant and when, growing food, planting for pollinators and making habitat for garden animals. The site offers this either in their educational garden or at your own school garden. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the educational garden with a facilitator, look at what is planted where and when it goes in, and work out what would grow in their own school garden.
programs.our_note: This is the one to pick if you already have beds at your centre and no idea what to do with them. They will also come to your garden instead, so ask which version you are being quoted for.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers. The price, the maximum group size and the notice period are not published, so call before you plan the day.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.
curriculum_tags: First Peoples concepts of interconnectedness in the environment
First Peoples knowledge of sustainable practices

programs.name: Water, Water Everywhere
programs.description: A 1.5 hour program for grades 2 to 7 on the role of water in the gardens, the nearby wetlands and the wider watershed, covering how plants drink through their roots, where rain goes and how dirty water is cleaned. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Follow water around the site with a facilitator, from plant roots in the garden beds out to the wetlands next door, and talk about where rainwater goes after it lands.
programs.our_note: It starts at grade 2, so this is not one for a daycare group. Wetlands mean wet feet in most months, so rubber boots are the difference between a good morning and a short one.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers, though the wetland part of the route is rougher. No price, group size limit or notice period is published, so call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.
curriculum_tags: First Peoples concepts of interconnectedness in the environment
First Peoples knowledge of sustainable practices

programs.name: Ethnobotany Explorations
programs.description: A 1.5 hour walk of the Ethnobotany Trail for grades 2 to 12, learning the Indigenous names and uses of native plants and discussing the importance of native ecosystems. The site describes it as taking place in W̱SÁNEĆ territory. Program fees include entrance into the gardens, and no dollar amount is published.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the Ethnobotany Trail with a guide, stopping at native plants to hear their Indigenous names and what they were and are used for.
programs.our_note: This is mostly walking and listening rather than doing, so it lands better with children who are already comfortable on a guided walk. It starts at grade 2 and runs to grade 12, so ask them to pitch it for your group.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers, though the trail itself is rougher going. The price, the group size limit and the notice period are not published, so call ahead.
programs.extra_fees_note: An optional 30 minute self guided activity in the gardens is available for an additional fee, and the amount is not published.
curriculum_tags: First Peoples concepts of interconnectedness in the environment
First Peoples knowledge of sustainable practices

programs.name: In School Presentation
programs.description: HCP comes to your classroom with lesson plans, all the materials for hands on classroom gardening activities and a facilitator. The site says the facilitation is currently virtual. Learning standards are shaped around what the teacher asks for. No age range, group size or fee is published.
programs.what_children_do: Take part in gardening activities in their own classroom using materials HCP brings or sends, with the facilitator leading the session.
programs.our_note: Useful when a bus is the thing standing between you and the outing. Ask plainly whether a person comes to the room or joins on a screen, because the page says the facilitation is currently virtual while the heading says in school.
programs.practical_summary: This one happens at your place, so washrooms, lunch and rain are your own arrangements. The fee, the age range and the notice period are not published, so ask when you get in touch.
programs.evidence: The classroom presentation includes lesson plans, all the materials to offer hands-on classroom gardening activities and HCP facilitation (currently virtual).

programs.name: Virtual Workshop
programs.description: A live classroom presentation delivered remotely along with a kit of materials, designed for teachers and their classes. Learning standards are based on what the teacher asks for. No age range, group size, duration or fee is published.
programs.what_children_do: Work through a plant activity in their own classroom using the kit that arrives, following a facilitator on screen.
programs.our_note: Worth asking what is actually in the kit and who has to set it up, since with a group of small children that job lands on you. Nothing about the fee or the notice needed is published, so email before you plan around it.
programs.practical_summary: This runs in your own room, so the practical side is yours to arrange. The fee, the age range and the lead time are all unpublished and worth asking about in the same message.
programs.evidence: The Virtual Classroom is a classroom presentation and kit.

programs.name: School tour
programs.description: A guided walk of the demonstration gardens and natural spaces for a group of students or teachers, showing the seasonal interests of the gardens and how the spaces can be used for teaching. No age range, duration, group size or fee is published for this option.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the demonstration gardens and the natural spaces, stopping to look at what is in season.
programs.our_note: This is the plain walk and look option rather than a facilitated lesson, so it suits a group that just wants the garden. Nothing about how long it takes or what it costs is published, so ask for both when you enquire.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers. Length, group size and price are all unpublished for this option, so treat the phone call as part of the planning.
programs.evidence: Our knowledgeable guide will take you on a beautiful journey through our demonstration gardens and natural spaces

programs.name: Master Gardener guided tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the gardens led by a Master Gardener from the Victoria Master Gardener Association, covering the gardens' highlights, Victoria's gardening history and growing tips for this climate. Flat rate pricing is by group size: $150.00 covers 6 to 12 people with one guide, and $360.00 covers 13 to 24 people with two guides. Groups of fewer than six are treated as private tours and are subject to availability. Tours typically last 45 to 60 minutes, and admission for the group leader and bus driver is included in the tour cost.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the gardens in a group behind a Master Gardener, stopping at the highlights while the guide talks about the plants and the site's history.
programs.our_note: The price is for the whole group, not per person, so a class of 20 pays $360 in total and gets two guides. It is a talk and walk aimed at general visitors rather than a children's program, so for under sevens the school programs will land better.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and most paths take strollers, though sloped sections take longer. Buses can drop off but cannot park, and no start times, notice period or booking address are published, so call to arrange it.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $150.00 rate covers a group of 6 to 12 with one guide. A group of 13 to 24 is $360.00 and comes with two guides. Admission for the group leader and the bus driver is included.
programs.evidence: $150.00 – Covers a group of 6 to 12 participants and includes one Master Gardener tour guide.

programs.name: Self guided garden visit
programs.description: The gardens are open to walk on your own every day from 9:00am to 4:00pm. Admission is $17.00 for adults over 16, $13.00 for seniors 60 and over and students with ID, and free for children under 16 and for HCP members. A member's guest accompanied by a member pays $11.00. The site says touring the gardens takes about an hour.
programs.what_children_do: Wander the paths through the display gardens at their own pace, take the Japanese and Zen garden loop, find the Children's Garden to play in and stop at the ponds and the wetland edges.
programs.our_note: Children under 16 are free, so the only real cost is the adults you bring. There is no booking route or group rate published for a self guided visit, so if you are arriving with a dozen children it is worth a call so they are not surprised at the front desk.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site, most paths take strollers with extra time on slopes, and there is no indoor space beyond a classroom portable used for programs. Buses can drop off but cannot park, and parking on site is limited.
programs.extra_fees_note: Seniors 60 and over and students with ID pay $13.00. A member's guest accompanied by a member pays $11.00.

gaps: no dollar amount is published for any school program; the schools page says only that program fees include entrance into the gardens
the optional 30 minute self guided activity added to a school program costs an additional fee, and the amount is not stated

the home learner page shows fees such as $90 for Garden Creatures, but those are for multi week home learner series with published dates, not for a single class visit, so they were not recorded as school program prices
no minimum notice or lead time for booking a school program is published
no maximum or minimum group size is published for any school program
no chaperone ratio or number of free adult places is published
no start times or days of the week are published for school programs
washrooms are described only inside a Garden Nature Academy program listing, as access to the lower classroom portable, so it is worth confirming that a visiting class can use them
no indoor lunch space is described; the hours page invites visitors to pack a picnic and find a shady nook, which is outdoors

rain backup was left unanswered because the shelter described is the lower classroom portable used by one specific children's program, while the hours page says the Gardens may close in inclement weather
the tours page publishes no start times or notice period for the Master Gardener tour

email addresses on the contact page are hidden by Cloudflare email protection in a plain fetch. They were read in a browser, where the page lists youthprograms@hcp.ca for youth, children and school groups and events@hcp.ca for tours

PRICE NOTE: a fetched copy of the hours and admission page served older admission prices of $16.00 adult, $12.00 senior and student and $9.00 member's guest. The live page shows $17.00, $13.00 and $11.00, and the live figures are the ones recorded here
the booking request link goes to an outside registration system and its address could not be captured, so email or phone is recorded as the booking route
a Mentoring option is listed on the schools page with no description, age range or fee, so it was not recorded as a program

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the HCP Kids landing page renders its program list in JavaScript and a plain fetch returns only the introduction. The navigation and the photographs are also JavaScript driven, and the photographs are CSS background images rather than picture tags, so a fetch only re-run will appear to find a much thinner site.
none of the photographs on the site carry alt text, so every alt here was written after looking at the image in a browser
the site publishes no Open Graph image, so the hero was taken from the tours page

COORDINATES: their site publishes two different points. The map embed on the contact page gives only the centre of the map view, and the hours and admission page links through to Google Maps with a pin on the gardens themselves. The point here is now that pin, 48.50121 and -123.41386. The value we had before was the view centre, about 100 m away, and it had been rounded down to four decimal places.
